skill.name: landing-page-design
skill.description: Design conversion-focused landing pages using practical guidance for headlines, hero sections, calls to action, social proof, forms, mobile layouts, and page speed.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline formatting. Confirmed risks are external package installation, third-party CLI execution, and transmission of prompts or search queries to remote services.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends installing external packages with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions and commits, document package provenance, and require user confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: The skill sends prompts and search queries to third-party services through belt.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose remote data processing and tell users to remove secrets, personal data, and confidential business information.

remediation.issue: The allowed Bash pattern permits any belt subcommand.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed commands to the required belt operations and require confirmation before login or remote execution.

content.value_statement: Visitors leave when a landing page lacks clear value, trust, or direction. This skill provides practical rules for persuasive, responsive, conversion-focused page design.
actual_capabilities: Structures above-the-fold content around a headline, supporting copy, one primary call to action, imagery, and social proof.
Provides formulas and examples for outcome-focused headlines and specific call-to-action text.
Recommends a complete section order covering benefits, proof, pricing, objections, and a final call to action.
Reviews forms, mobile layouts, image sizing, and page speed against stated design targets.
Generates example prompts for hero images, social sharing images, and conversion research through the optional belt CLI.
limitations: It provides design guidance but does not build, deploy, or test a complete landing page by itself.
Conversion recommendations are general and must be validated with audience research and controlled experiments.
AI image and web research examples require the external belt CLI, an account, and remote services.
Several quantitative claims are presented without citations and may vary by market, device, or traffic source.

use_cases.title: Plan a Startup Launch Page
use_cases.description: Create a focused page outline with clear messaging, trust signals, and a primary signup action.

use_cases.title: Improve a SaaS Conversion Path
use_cases.description: Review page sections, calls to action, forms, and mobile behavior for conversion obstacles.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Responsive Design Brief
use_cases.description: Translate product outcomes into layout, content, imagery, and performance requirements for implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Hero Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a landing page hero for [product]. The audience is [audience], the main problem is [problem], and the desired action is [action].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting a new landing page.

prompt_templates.title: Organize the Full Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a section outline for [product]. Include value, social proof, benefits, process, testimonials, pricing, objections, and a final call to action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this after the core offer and audience are defined.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this landing page content: [content]. Identify unclear messaging, weak proof, competing actions, form friction, mobile issues, and performance risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to improve an existing page before testing.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Test Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized experiment plan for [page]. Use [traffic data], [audience research], and [business goal]. Define hypotheses, metrics, variants, and stopping rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced conversion optimization with reliable evidence.

output_examples.input: Draft a hero for an automated documentation product used by small engineering teams.
output_examples.output: Headline: Ship accurate documentation before every release. Supporting copy: Turn code changes into clear documentation without adding another manual review step. Action: Create your first guide.

output_examples.input: Outline a landing page for a customer feedback analysis service.
output: Hero: State the outcome and offer one trial action.
Proof: Show customer logos and a verified analysis result.
Benefits: Explain faster prioritization, shared evidence, and fewer manual reviews.
Process: Connect sources, classify feedback, and share priorities.

output_examples.input: Audit a mobile signup form with six required fields and a small submit button.
output_examples.output: Reduce the form to essential signup details, use a single column, enlarge tap targets, add inline validation, and replace generic submit text.

best_practices: Define one audience, one desired outcome, and one primary action before writing the page.
Support every major claim with verifiable customer evidence, product data, or a clearly labeled source.
Test responsive layout, accessibility, loading performance, and conversion behavior with real devices and representative traffic.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague headlines that describe technology without naming a customer outcome.
Do not present several actions with equal visual weight near the primary conversion point.
Do not send confidential prompts, customer data, or unpublished strategy to external generation and search services.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete landing page?
faq.answer: It creates design direction, copy options, section structure, and review criteria. Implementation still requires a web development workflow.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing page?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the page content, audience, business goal, available evidence, and known performance data for a focused audit.

faq.question: Does it require the belt CLI?
faq.answer: No for design guidance. Belt is required only for the included remote image generation and research examples.

faq.question: Will the recommendations guarantee higher conversions?
faq.answer: No. Use the recommendations as hypotheses, then validate them through research, analytics, usability testing, and controlled experiments.

faq.question: Does it cover mobile design?
faq.answer: Yes. It addresses tap targets, form layout, typography, responsive images, horizontal overflow, and access to the primary action.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Remove secrets, personal data, and confidential business details before using any external image generation or research service.
